newsitem.title: GERMANY: Soyoil use in Europe could fall due to gene fears.
newsitem.headline: Soyoil use in Europe could fall due to gene fears.

text.p: Soyoil could lose out to rapeseed oil in Europe if more processors shun soy oil due to possible use of genetically-modified U.S. soybeans, German grain trade paper Ernaehrungsdienst (ED) said on Wednesday.
"At the moment, this is not yet a factor but rape oil demand in Rotterdam should rise sooner or later," ED said.

Last Friday, the German subsidiary of food group Nestle said it would not use soy products derived from the new U.S. beans from the 1996/97 harvest which consumer and environmentalist group have associated with unknown risks.
A day earlier, the German unit of Anglo-Dutch group Unilever said it would not sell products containing oils from the new beans.

In Rotterdam on Wednesday rape oil was at a 2.50 guilder premium over soy oil at 91.50 guilders per 100 kilos for Nov/Jan material. Rapeseed last traded at a steady 467.50-470 marks free Hamburg, ED reported.

The Hamburg-based independent newsletter Oil World said the premium was likely to be maintained in the campaign against soybeans, at least in Germany, with lower rapeseed supply another factor in the equation.

The premium is hurting EU export markets for rape oil as traditional consumers in North Africa and elsewhere are shifting to lower priced soy and sunflower oils, it said. --Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
